pulse-duration.comment: Canonical loop duration for `.device-loading-notice`, `.plan-card__stepped-direction`, and `.plan-card__stepped-seg[data-pulse="true"]` opacity/transform pulses in style.css. Replaces three near-identical literals (1.4s / 1.5s / 1.6s) that produced perceptually indistinguishable cadence — single source of truth for any future tuning. Literal duration (not an alias) — pulse cadence is a perceptual constant, not theme-relative.

selected-indicator-color.comment: M3 underline-indicator colour for the selected nav tab. The selected tab now reads as a modern M3 tab strip — an accent underline bar plus a primary-text label — rather than a filled pill. Accent (brand green) is the canonical M3 active-indicator colour and stays distinct from the tonal segmented-control fill used elsewhere.

selected-indicator-height.comment: M3 primary-tab active-indicator thickness (3 px is the Material 3 spec value). Literal px — there is no 3 px spacing step and the indicator is a fixed hairline bar, not layout spacing, so it is encoded directly at the token layer.

selected-background.comment: The selected nav tab no longer fills a pill — it uses the M3 underline indicator (`selected-indicator-color`) plus a primary-text label, so the tab container stays transparent (the base `.tabs` rule already paints no container fill). Retained as the documented selected-state anchor for the strip; the layout test pins it to `transparent` to guard against a pill regression, and the `selected-hover-background` sibling is still consumed by `.plan-chip--link` hover.

selected-hover-background.comment: Tonal accent-tint hover fill. No longer used by the nav tab (which is underline-only) but still consumed by `.plan-chip--link[aria-pressed=true]:hover`, so the token stays.

control-track-3x.comment: Three touch-target slots wide. Encoded as the absolute px value because Style Dictionary cannot resolve a calc against another token at build time; keep in sync with pels.touch-target.min (currently 48 px) so this stays equal to 3 * pels.touch-target.min.

actual.comment: SEMANTIC DATA-VIZ PALETTE — one hue, one meaning across every chart: mint (`color.role.good`) = actual / measured / delivered / picked; dim mint (`color.base.viz.mint-dim`) = measured totals carrying no managed/background claim; ice-blue (`color.base.viz.ice`) = projection / plan / forecast; amber (`pels.chart.warn`) = warning only; red (`pels.chart.danger`) = error / over-hard-cap only; slate (`color.base.viz.slate`) = background / neutral, with `viz.slate-bright` for dashed reference strokes. Auxiliary identities that sit outside the series family and keep their own meaning: purple = money/price axis (`price-line`), and the price-LEVEL tones on the hour strips (`hour-tone-*`). No chart may introduce a hue outside this set. This token: the Actual (measured) stroke on the Budget charts — previously the near-white text tone.

plan.comment: Planned hourly allocation bars (Budget hourly chart's single-series legacy path, when no managed/background split exists). Ice-blue — the palette's plan/forecast family. The dashed budget REFERENCE stroke is `pels.chart.budget-reference`, not this.

budget-reference.comment: Dashed budget reference strokes: the Budget progress chart's budget-pace line and the Usage daily chart's budget markLine, plus their legend swatches and label pills. A reference is a neutral guideline, not a judgment — so it is slate, never amber (amber = warning only).

measured.comment: Measured totals without a managed/background claim: the Usage day chart's fallback bars, the typical-day and hourly-pattern averages, and the daily-history bars. One dim/desaturated step below the managed mint so a mixed day (split hours next to fallback hours) can't read fallback columns as 'fully managed'. Previously the saturated grass-green accent.

managed.comment: Managed (PELS-influenceable) share of a usage split. Mint — the same family the Overview hero's managed power segment uses (`--pels-status-good`), so 'managed' reads as one colour across the hero bar, the Budget hourly stack, and the Usage stack. Previously `color.role.warn`, which collided with the amber `pels.chart.warn` unreliable-hour encoding.

background.comment: Background (non-managed) share of a usage split. Neutral slate; its own viz value (same rendered colour as the former `color.semantic.text.muted` alias) so a future text-tone tweak can't silently recolor three charts. Deliberately NOT `color.role.info`, which the semantic viz palette reserves for projection/forecast.

picked.comment: Hours a smart task picked, on the schedule chart: picked hours render as filled mint bars, non-picked hours as the same hue dimmed/outlined (opacity derived in-chart). Mint = the palette's 'picked/delivered' meaning; the bar height already carries the price, so price-level colour-coding stays off this chart.

forecast.comment: Projection / forecast strokes (Budget progress projection, comparison forecasts). Dotted ice-blue per the semantic viz palette — quiet, provisional ink, distinct from the saturated info-blue status tone.

heatmap-high.comment: Power-week heatmap ramp = measured energy, so it runs surface→mint (the palette's measured family). Previously the saturated grass-green accent, which sat outside the semantic viz set.

unattributed.comment: Usage-stack segment for measured energy the managed/background split does not attribute (gross tracking gap). One surface step above `disabled-bar` so the claim-free region is visible against the plot without claiming a meaning; deliberately off-legend — the tapped readout carries the exact numbers.

cell-radius.comment: Heatmap-cell corner radius shared by powerWeekChartEcharts.ts (ECharts `borderRadius`) and `.usage-legend__swatch--unreliable`. Promoted from a parallel `--radius-xs` literal so the legend/cell shape contract is enforced at the chart token layer.

week-height.comment: Power-week heatmap container height shared by `.power-week-chart` in style.css (height/min-height) and `resolveChartHeight` in powerWeekChartEcharts.ts (ECharts viewport via `initEcharts`/`chart.resize`). Promoted from parallel `240px` / `240` literals so the container box and the SVG viewport cannot drift. Literal value (not an alias) — chart heights are physical-pixel, not theme-relative; cf. `.deadline-horizon-chart`.
